land.text: Dutch Suriname, from 1954 a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, independent on 25 November 1975 (the dutch-suriname dossier dissolves on that date with this state as counterpart)

predecessors.note: Reviewer fix (am-08-k review): the predecessor dossier is dutch-suriname (1667-1975), whose dissolve event of November 1975 names republic-of-suriname; the netherlands-antilles dossier (am-06) already removes Suriname from Cliopatria's 1877-2023 'Netherlands Antilles' shape and has no 1975 event. 'In 1954, Suriname became one of the constituent countries of the Kingdom of the Netherlands'; the Dutch 'retained control of its defence and foreign affairs'.

capitals.name: Paramaribo
capitals.note: 'The capital and largest city is Paramaribo.'

correction.text: the 1976 shape unchanged, carried back to independence: 'On 25 November 1975, it became independent following negotiations with the Dutch government'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Suriname row begins in 1976 but the page dates independence to 25 November 1975.

146,979 km2 against the infobox 165,940 km2 (ratio 0.89, within a factor of two). The polygon is 541 cells against 539 for Natural Earth's Suriname (17 cells sit beyond the country along the Corantijn, 15 country cells are missed), shares no cell with the Guyana shape, so the New River Triangle stays Guyanese. 'Guyana' in the seed's modern_countries is that river-edge spill.

region.text: Suriname, the former Dutch Guiana, between the Corantijn and the Marowijne

ledger.note: 25 November 1975: Suriname becomes independent from the Netherlands. 'On 25 November 1975, it became independent following negotiations with the Dutch government.' The land passes from dutch-suriname (dissolved 25 November 1975 with this state as counterpart); Cliopatria draws Dutch Suriname inside its Netherlands Antilles row, which the netherlands-antilles dossier corrects.
25 February 1980: a military coup overthrows Arron's government, led by Dési Bouterse; same state, same land. 'On 25 February 1980, a military coup overthrew Arron's government.'

wars.name: Suriname Interior War (Maroon rebellion)
wars.outcome: The page says only that the civil war 'begun in 1986, continued' and gives no end date or territorial result.
wars.note: 'The brutal civil war between the Suriname army and Maroons loyal to rebel leader Ronnie Brunswijk, begun in 1986, continued...' The 'to' year is the start year because the page is silent on the end; whether the rebels held land is not stated, so no rebel dossier or contest event is written.

certainty.note: Frontiers are river lines. Disputed: the New River Triangle with Guyana (Guyana holds it), the Marowijne border with French Guiana ('disputed along the Marowijne River') and the maritime boundary with Guyana, part of which the Permanent Court of Arbitration decided on 20 September 2007.

sources.title: Suriname
sources.note: Identity, infobox area 165,940 km2, Paramaribo, independence 25 November 1975, 1954 constituent country, 1980 coup, 1986 civil war, border disputes.

sources.title: New River Triangle
sources.note: Background only: the Tigri Area clashes of 1967-1969 (recorded in the guyana dossier) and Suriname's claim that passed to the new state.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Netherlands Antilles' 1877-2023 shape (149,155 km2, modern countries Suriname and Guyana) is Suriname's outline, so the Suriname row overlaps it fully from 1976 to 2023 (541 cells); the netherlands-antilles dossier (am-06) already removes Suriname from that shape after 1845, and the predecessor is dutch-suriname (reviewer fix). The native name 'Republiek Suriname' is not on the page (the page gives only 'officially the Republic of Suriname'). The page budget (1-2) is met. The 1967-1969 Tigri Area (New River Triangle) clashes predate the state and are recorded in the guyana dossier (contest events and a war); 'Prior to Suriname's independence in 1975, President Henck Arron asked' the Dutch Prime Minister to define the border and the reply included the Tigri area (New River Triangle page), so the claim passed to the new state, which holds none of the Triangle. No gain or loss after 1975: the New River Triangle (Guyana-held) and the Marowijne river border with French Guiana are claims and river lines the pages leave unchanged; the 1986 Maroon war has no dated territorial result on the page. Gazetteer: Tigri Area / New River Triangle (region) is needed; see the guyana dossier.
